note: The pinned cross-host CLI contract for the one verb this host shares with the
TypeScript front-end. Each case names an argv, the exit code both CLIs return, and
Normalisation drops the diagnostic MESSAGE and keeps the code and the path. That is
deliberate and is the substantive claim: the wire contract fixes the error code
vocabulary and the $-rooted path, and every conformant host must agree on those; the
message is host-worded by design (the reference front-end's INVALID_JSON message
carries its own parser's expectation, which no other host could reproduce without
copying that parser). A diff over messages would fail on a difference the
specification licenses, and would have to be relaxed the first time it ran.
'out' is the exact stdout of the plain (non-JSON) form where the two hosts agree on
it byte for byte, and null where they do not - which is only the case whose message
is host-worded. Where 'out' is null the exit code and the normalised report still
tests/test_cli_parity.py checks this file BOTH ways: this host must satisfy it on
every run, and in a cross-host checkout with a built reference CLI the reference must
satisfy it too - so the pin cannot quietly rot into a description of one host.
outOfContract: An unrecognised flag: the reference front-end skips it and validates anyway; this
host refuses with exit 2, on the reasoning the estate's other validator CLI uses (a
silently-ignored --json is a report the caller believes it asked for and did not
get). A deliberate divergence, so no case pins it.
